Greetings!

I am a member of the Order of the Chronographs, a special department within the Historians' organization.

Our task is to continuously document all the information that comes to us. Any data will be recorded and subsequently transferred for general use to the archive on the Nea allod where our permanent base is located.

Well, the value of such data is difficult to underestimate, because this is the story of the creator of the gods herself. Of course, as historians, we must approach everything with skepticism, but this narrative is very important as an outsider's view of the struggle between Nihaz and Sarn.

"All that has been created will perish.

All that has perished will be recreated.

The existence is a great circle. There is no creation without destruction. There is no destruction without creation.

The circle has no beginning or end.

The divine couple has always existed: the All-Mother and Father Time. I, All-Mother, is the goddess of life and creation. Father Time is the god of death and destruction. Together we led our worlds through the cycles of births and deaths. We created and destroyed.

We were not alone. Our passion gave birth to our divine children, subject to us. Each of them played their own role. Each of them obeyed the universal laws. There were twelve Domains in my hierarchy. Each Domain was responsible for a single power. Each Domain had a master.

Only I, the All-Mother, the goddess of creation, and my divine husband Father Time, the god of destruction, were eternal Lords of our Domains. Other gods were immortal and lived very long lives which ultimately had to end. The circle kept going, and gods were destined to die.

Many years have passed."

"Each world was once created. At the moment of creation its death was predefined. Father Time knows no pity. He watches the sand of time in his hourglass.

There's a point in the circle that is called Judgment Time. Ancient prophecies come true. War is raging in multiple worlds. The Twilight of the Gods is imminent. This is the time when the figures on the board change. The wheel turns. Those who was on top will fall. Those who were beneath will rise.

This is the fate of the world predetermined by me, the All-Mother, and by Father Time. Evil against Good. Evil rises over Good for just an instant but its fate is predetermined as well. It will fall. The Good will win, there is no other way. The sacrifice is great, but after night comes day. This is the law that we established.

This is what happened last time. The ancient God of Darkness, now known as the Forgotten, has risen in all of his power. The worlds are burning, seized by the legions of Darkness. But the God of Light Sarn has also risen. He led the resistance against the Darkness and destroyed the Forgotten once and for all. This was predetermined. Everything happened just as we had planned.

The new day has come. The circle is turning once again."

"Many gods fell in the war with the Forgotten. Many worlds were destroyed. The survivors gathered in Eidos where the primal images of creation are stored. Everything that had to be created originally existed in Eidos.

I set to work, creating new worlds to replace what was destroyed. I created the twelve inner worlds first, in accordance with the number of Domains. Each of them should have been led by one of the survivors or newly born gods.

Sarn was one of the survivors, the greatest hero of the past war. He rightfully took the place of the God of Light.

Father Time and I chose two young goddesses among the new gods: Hirkalla and Hinanna. They were supposed to lead the Domains of Life and Death.

Only the Domain of the Forgotten, the Domain of Darkness remained without a ruler. None of the surviving gods wanted the responsibility."

"Millions of years passed since the victory over the Forgotten. The new god of the Domain of Darkness appeared. Hinanna, the younger sister, brought him to the door of Eidos. We accepted him and allowed him to take the vacant place. Each of the gods was supposed to played a role. The God of Darkness was accepted in our domain.

Hinanna's decision did not surprise me. She was a beautiful young goddess who was also stubborn, moody, gullible, and impulsive. She traveled the worlds a lot, found her chosen ones among gods and mortals, toyed with their lives.

At some point, the mysterious God of Darkness attracted her attention. No one knew where he had come from. Some thought he was a mortal who managed to become a god. This was extremely rare back then.

Hinanna showed him the way to Eidos, even though her sister Hirkalla warned her that his intentions weren't pure. There was something sinister about the traveler, so she decided to keep an eye on him."

"Hinanna was happy to see new faces. She and Nihaz, the God of Darkness, traveled between worlds, watched the fates of mortals, learned their secrets, discovered ancient artifacts of past eons.

The power of the new God of Darkness grew by the year. Ancient monsters, who still remembered the Forgotten, accepted him. None of us had any objections. The Darkness was the natural opposite of the Light, and the Domain required a master. At that time Father Time and I considered him an ordinary "Master of Darkness," one of many. As other gods, he was supposed to start a war and fight the Light, and finally perish, like the Forgotten before him. This is what we thought, so we never worried.

Only Hirkalla sensed that the circle has changed. We considered her too young to rule the Domain of Death. She was in charge of the Guardians of Ganzir who ruled the postmortal fates of all living in our worlds. Thanks to this, she saw that Nihaz was helping, teaching, and protecting mortals as best he could in his travels with Hinanna. She realized that their faith in him gave him even more power."

"In doubt, Hirkalla decided to talk to him. She gathered herself, and went to the throne of Darkness to dispel her fears. At that time, Hinanna took interest in another mortal, and the God of Darkness was left alone.

They had a long conversation. Hirkalla voiced her doubts, and Nihaz answered them. Few people knew what they were talking about, but Hinanna returned from her journey and witnessed the end of the talk.

The younger sister learned that Nihaz wanted to overthrow me and Father Time. He considered our concept of the world despicable. He mocked the idea of the circle and the renewal of worlds. Nihaz believed that the gods should make mortals our equals, teach them the laws of creation and eternal life.

Hinanna rushed to our divine throne straight away to warn us of the betrayal. I was furious. I ordered that Hirkalla be brought before me."

"She was brought to us, and we condemned her for her disobedience. She silently accepted it and went to live in exile. Since that day, Nihaz was unwelcome in Eidos. Unfortunately, by that time many of the gods were on his side. The creators that didn't want the destruction of their worlds listened to him. This rebel was loved not only by those who belonged to the Darkness but also those from the Domains of Chaos and Death. Even gods of elements joined the rebellion.

I didn't expect him to turn to mortals, helping them fight monsters and improving their lives. His was praised for giving knowledge and teaching crafts. Nihaz's gifts were poisonous, but he gave them generously to his followers. Mortals who sought immortality and divinity all rebelled.

Anxiously we have watched from our thrones the growing numbers of Nihaz's army. There was still time until another cycle of destruction and rebirth, but this war couldn't wait. It came to us."

"Hirkalla, our beloved daughter, then joined Nihaz. With all her heart, she accepted his teaching about the freedom of choice, the breaking of the great circle, and giving the mortals freedom to become gods.

Our worlds were thrown in a long war. Nihaz and the other gods fought against me and Father Time. Sarn, the God of Light, was one of his main enemies in this war.

Nihaz's efforts bore fruit. Gods died one after another. The most terrible thing happened when Nihaz and the others dealt a fatal blow to Father Time. They overcome him near the World of Destruction where he engaged in a battle with the Darkness. Only a God can kill a God. Nihaz dealt a fatal blow to Father Time who was already wounded, then took away his power. Since then, he became something greater than the God of Darkness, but he did not achieve what was after."

"'We were wondering what he really wanted. Sarn suggested that his true goal was to become more powerful. He destroyed many gods, including his former allies, Gods of Death and Chaos, and took their power.

Disturbed by what happened to my husband, I started to avoid battles. Eden, the world of Life, became my shelter. The story was simple. I knew that my daughter Hinanna would gain enough experience and wisdom to eventually become the ruler of the divine garden. The Garden of Eden was hidden from Nihaz. Everyone was safe. The war was continued by Sarn, Nihaz's complete opposite. He successfully destroyed legions of darkness marching through our worlds.

But even a great warrior can be betrayed. There was a traitor in our ranks. To my surprise, it was Hinanna. Jealous of her sister and the glory she achieved by serving Nihaz, she decided to chain sides. Hinanna lured Sarn into a trap. After fighting Nihaz, the God of Light was captured."

"Hinanna strove to be equal to her elder sister. She strove to surpass her. At that time Hirkalla already possessed the power of Darkness and ruled the World of Death. Jealous of her sister's might, Hinanna wanted to seize what she possessed.

She gathered secret forces, wore her best clothes and jewelry, and embarked on the journey. She approached the colossal gates of the underground world, awoke the guardian by banging on the doors, and fiercely demanded that he let her in.

But one cannot enter this world without obeying its laws. Hinanna had to give all her clothes and jewels along with all her powers to pass the gates of Ganzir. And she fell under the power of the World of Death ruled by her sister. The young goddess never expected this. She was dead while still being alive, condemned to the worst fate imaginable.

I knew not what became of Sarn. I knew not of the fate of the younger daughter. Although I felt sorry for the gullible Hinanna that fell victim to her own stupidity, there was a much worse threat hanging over our worlds. The Architect came from a faraway world. The heartless Order where mind and will were one. Nihaz and I had to fight the invader.

I came out of my shelter every once in a while. Having destroyed an emissary of the new enemy, I felt that my lost daughter and a forgotten friend were once again close. When the ship of the missionary of the Order was torn to pieces by my Great Trees, he fell like a ball of fire upon the lifeless world. I gazed upon the barren land and saw only vile dragons loyal to Nihaz. I realized that they would summon their King, so I left this world. I returned to Eden but never gave up my attempts at finding my lost daughter.

What is mortals' time to me? A blink. It's been five thousand years. My heart is still yearning."
This information was collected during the Great Ball on Irene... An interesting document written by Adele de Ardeur. I can show it to you.

The note in neat handwriting reads:

The Great Ball is a demonstration of the accomplishments of all the Elven Great Houses. At each of the Great Balls, one of the Houses showed something grandiose. It all began when the Elves recovered from the past Cataclysm, created portals on their allods, and started visiting each other.

Year 265, House de Doucer wins. Great Mage Gramont de Douceur, with the consent of the other Heads of the Houses, creates new rules for the Great Balls. The first Great Ball takes place on the Yoggor allod.

Year 275, House de Vevre wins, Orelina de Vevre writes the poem "The World's End" that describes the history of the Cataclysm and the subsequent events. The second Great Ball was also held on the Yoggor allod, but later it was decided to hold the Ball on the allod of the winner of the last Ball.

The note in neat handwriting reads:

Year 305, House de Desirae wins, Great Mage Margot de Desirae writes "Dialogues on Service", substantiating a point of view that explains why the Elves should educate lower races and have them serve the Elves. Those who are resistant to training (humans in particular) should be avoided.

Year 319, House de Blizare wins. Great Mage Bernard de Blizare creates "The Treatise on the Essence of the Astral", with a theoretical substantiation of the existence of the Astral.

Year 335, House de Grandeur wins, Vincent de Grandeur creates "The Book of Astral Curses" which summarizes all known spells associated with the Astral.

Year 364, House de Delice wins. Ervier de Delice invents a stable stationary portal between the allods that allows you to travel in a relatively simple way, albeit with a colossal expenditure of magical energy.

Year 384, House de Desirae wins. Viola di Desirae writes "Odes of Love", a collection of the greatest elven love lyrics.

The note in neat handwriting reads:

Year 404, House de Delice wins. Florian de Delice finds a solution to the dispute between the elven Houses and settles the conflict over territory.

Year 419, House de Doucer wins, Renalda de Doucer restores the list of ancient elven spells found on Yoggor.

Year 443, House de Delice wins, Florian de Delice solves the problem of settling the status of the Small elven Houses.

Year 464, House de Pluie wins. Thibault de Pluie creates an economic treatise on trade, banks and auctions.

Year 479, House de Ardeur wins, Gaben de Ardeur makes a breakthrough in the study of the properties of June crystals.

Year 499, House de Pluie wins, Gracienna de Pluie creates a unique piece of jewelry - the Diadem of Drops.

The note in neat handwriting reads:

Year 515, House de Blizare wins, Justine de Blizare completes a study on the influence of the Astral on the flora and fauna of allods.

Year 538, House de Vevre wins. Majel de Vevre writes an opera about Irene, one of the greatest works in the genre.

Year 556, House de Grandeur wins, Neven de Grandeur writes a work on the history of magic from the founding of the elven kingdom to the present day.

Year 583, House de Desirae wins, Rival de Desirae creates a ten-ingredient salad recipe.

Year 596, House de Delice wins. Denise de Delice paints one of the most beautiful paintings in history - The Birth of Beauty, depicting the awakening of the first elves.

It's a unique chronicle in a special style. There are a few embellishments, of course, but it tells us about the history of the North and Isa. It's good that you've heard it. Now everyone can hear it.

Evil storms raged,

White snow fell,

The house stood strong,

Steady and unshakeable.

He who was the oldest

Among the harsh leaders,

Became a father for the first time -

To three brothers.

Thorri was the first,

Lok was next,

Wald came last,

Votin was their father.

Three Gibberlings -

Their sprout was strong!

It was noisy in the house,

Fun every day!

The children were growing up,

Year after year.

Thorri boasted of his strength,

Lok was the most cunning of all.

Wald loved to listen,

Sitting next to his father:

What others say,

Who believes what.

Who brings news

To their home.

To his uncles and aunt,

Of a different kind.

Braiding threads

In wonderful patterns,

She saw clearly

Signs and omens

In the Fabric of the Universe.

Numerous Orcs

Were slain by Thorri's hammer.

Scarlet flowers

Bloomed on Isa's snow.

The Gibberlings' fury

Spared no Orc.

In a terrible panic.

It is true that in unity

Was the Gibberlings' strength!

Wonderful armor,

Marvelous weapons!

They would have something to show

To Votin and the others!

In conversation.

Died in flames.

To Isa as a horde.

The brothers were quiet

For the next part of the journey.

They thought about Orcs,

Humans, and dragons.

The home was now

More weapons

Talking all the while

About upcoming battles.

Look - they are home!

In celebration of another victory,

A feast was held.

Brothers were honored,

With raised cups.

Many Gibberlings

Drank beer there,

Ate fish

And a lot of cheese.

And tales were told,

Each better than the last,

Around the mead hall

Deep into the night.

In the morning, early,

When it's dark,

And the fog is still

Over the water,

Three brothers left the house

And went to the square.

They saw a maiden there,

Black as midnight.

"I ask you to hear

What the Threads promise us."

They will carry your feat

That threaten the whole of Isa.

Horrible fate awaits us!

The power of insidious Fate!

The Threads of the universe

Tell me this:

Soon the world will plunge

Into the void of oblivion!

The roots of the world will crack,

Rocks will fall into the abyss,

And sea waters

Will boil all at once.

The wolf will swallow the sun,

And the stars will die out.

Darkness will swallow Isa,

Devouring everything.

Many souls will die,

Many words will be forgotten,

And the people of Isa

Will perish in the pitch darkness!

"Isa will survive!

From the wreckage of the old ones,

Will be our salvation.

Centuries later

Trouble will come again,

Darkness will cover the whole world.

The tree is dying,

The ancient enemy has been awakened,

There is no rest for the dead!

Deadly Frost will come,

And countless enemies

Whose skin is white.

I see it through time.

Blood ties get stronger:

Pilgrim's children

Will take ragged weaving

And tie it into a whole.

And the flower of hope

Will bloom at the Tree,

The news will rush further

To the wonderful land of stars.

This is just the beginning.

I see an ominous city,

It is full of the dead,

Summoned against their will.

Light and darkness in battle

Argue with each other,

But in vain:

Their fate is inevitable.

A new god will rise -

He who took the power

From the unfortunate sisters

Who forgot the law:

What Fate decides

Will happen.

That would change that."

Speeches have faded.

The Gibberling brothers

Conferred for a long time.

"You won't scare us!"

Thorri said,

"While my hammer is in my hand,

I will not accept this fate!"

"If the pattern is known,

And not yet woven...

We must take the Threads into our hands

And fool Fate!"

So said Lok,

The cunning trickster.

Wald, after much thought,

Supported the idea.

"Since Seida does not know

How to avoid Fate,

We will seek advice

From other peoples."

So it was decided,

And there was no reason to delay.

On the same day, the three brothers

Set off on another journey.

The path took them far away,

To the foot of Muspel

Where good Heidruns

Settled among the grass.

The Gibberlings were greeted

By Ilko, the chief of the horned ones.

The people welcomed the guests,

Offering mead.

"Tell us, wise one,

How to argue with Destiny?

How to avoid Fate,

What do the Threads say?"

The Heidrun chief said,

"Yes, Fate is harsh.

What it decided to weave

Will surely happen.

We gave this evil force

A different name.

We call it the Weaver

That spins Threads.

But we believe

That another power exists.

It gives a chance

To those it favors.

If Luck loves

Her chosen one,

They will avoid Fate

And deceive the Threads.

But while she falls in love quickly,

She falls out of it just as easily.

The circle will come around again,

And luck will pass."

"In our villages

We have these maidens.

Amorous for a day only,

And then - nothing,"

Lok said jokingly.

The brothers nodded:

"This is no good!

We need a sure way!"

Ilko thought for a while,

Then said,

"If you don't wish to wait

For the Star of Fortune...

There are other sagas

Which sing about marvels

About the one who created

All the living things.

He rarely appeared,

But whoever saw him knows:

Num is the creator of the living.

He must be wiser than all of us."

"That's right, Ilko,

Since he is the father to all of us,

He must know for real,

How to escape fate.

How do we find

Num who is invisible?

If he has a house,

Maybe that's where he is?"

Wise Ilko said,

"Num's house is unknown.

But there are signs

That can show the way.

When you see a Rainbow,

He is at the edge

Farthest from you.

Look there.

Where the sky shines,

From horizon to horizon,

Num will be close,

You can find him.

Where the winds were born

And the fires of volcanoes,

There are traces of creation,

And Num's abode.

But those brave ones

Who do not believe in fate

And who want to fight it

Should remember this:

By challenging the might

That is stronger than gods,

Brave madmen

Will bring doom."

"We will not be stopped

By threats of Fate,

A warrior does not fear

Empty words,"

So saying,

The warriors left.

The path took them far away,

To a place full of signs.

The north received the brothers,

Where the radiance of the sky

Illuminates the earth

But does not warm it.

The path is long and difficult,

The journey takes many days.

There is nothing but ice and rocks,

And spoils are scarce.

Every day is shorter

Under the dim sun,

The night grows boundlessly,

Darkness brings cold.

One night a storm

Wakes up the brothers.

A veil of snow

Covers everything around them.

They see through the snowstorm

That someone is approaching -

A silhouette

With a shaky gait.

Once the fire dispelled

The darkness that hid the image,

The brothers were horrified:

It was a frozen corpse!

Features and clan marks were hidden

Under the iron mask.

His armor was covered

With hoarfrost patterns.

Thorri swung his hammer

At the evil spirit!

But suddenly the uninvited guest

Said quietly,

"Who are you and why are you here?"

The brothers were surprised.

"We are Gibberlings

Looking for the house of Num."

"Like you, I once searched

For the House of the Creator...

The road was not easy,

I fell, killed by Frost."

"We do not fear Frost!"

Thorri answered.

"It is worth fearing

The Evil God of Cold.

Here he reigns supreme,

Eradicating life.

The deadly frost

Kills outright.

Be afraid to meet

The ice maiden here.

If you look even once

Into the eyes of an Isfrun,

You will turn to ice,

And your life force will fade.

Even the Junes fear

The powers of the harsh ice.

There are many other

Creatures of nightmare here.

Ice worms,

Jotunns and Wargs...

If you go further,

It will be even more dangerous.

Icy expanses

Are not for the living!"

"We will reach our goal,"

Said the brothers.

"The Threads of our Fate

Have become stronger!

Thank you for your advice...

What is your name?"

The dead one told them,

"They used to call me Nagle."

As the storm subsided,

They said goodbye to the guest,

And set out.

Many days passed.

Thorri often lifted

The hammer when necessary.

Many different creatures,

Some of them nameless,

He struck down with a blow,

Powerful and brave.

Lok scouted out the land.

With his cunning tricks,

He sneaked into the dwellings

Of snow giants.

After stealing food,

He returned to his brothers.

Wald, full of advice,

Knew the habits of monsters

And taught his brothers

How to avoid them.

Thus they reached the sea.

The end of their journey was close.

Massive mountains nearby

Were the borders of this world.

There, in the distance,

Burned a flame brighter than the sun.

It was their destination,

The end of distant wanderings.

The brothers found there

A strange old man

With a white beard,

Wearing scarlet clothes.

"Are you called Num?"

Lok asked fearlessly.

"Teach us, old one,

How to avoid Fate!"

"Foolish children!"

Num said angrily.

"In vain

You came to my halls!

I do know of a way

To avoid fate.

But it is infeasible

For the Sparks of mortals!

To argue with fate,

You must be free

Of all the chains

And fetters of the world.

But you are held tightly

By the Thread of Fate,

A vigilant Weaver

Spun it before your birth."

The brothers listened,

And in heavy thoughts

Set out for home.

Their families were waiting.

The threshold is in sight.

Within reach...

But wait, listen -

Bells are ringing!

This means the Orcs

Attacked viciously again.

The brothers did not wait -

Rushed to help!

A hard-won victory -

The brothers survived

Miraculously in this battle.

Such is the will of Fate!

Accepting the Threads,

The Gibberling brothers

Resigned themselves

To their great fate.

Future alliances

Needed a base

They were destined to build.

Votin gave Thorri

His mighty troops,

Lok will appease the Zvergs.

Wald will think of a way

To approach the harsh Pridens.

Great-grandchildren will continue

Their Threads in the Pattern.

What is meant to be will happen!

The Orcs will be gone from Isa!

Sagas will remember

Thorri, Lok, and Wald!

The glory of the Gibberlings

Is preserved for centuries!
